sentences.beta: In the reason field, explain WHY the equality you stated holds, by a relation among lengths of segments between the given points that holds for every position of P_x and is not merely an equality of two lengths. State that relation explicitly, in the given symbols.
sentences.proof: Finally, in the reason field, also prove that, as P_x moves on h1, the point P_y moves on a parabola. Give the proof as a chain of relations among the given points, ending with an equation that every position of P_y satisfies.
sentences.block: Do not use the fact that P_y is equidistant from F and from the line e: do not use P_yF = P_yK, and do not use that m is the perpendicular bisector of FK. Derive the equation from other relations among the given points.
sentences.form: Note: in the manner of Menaechmus and Newton, state the invariant as a PROPORTION (a mean proportional), not as an equality of lengths.
sentences.conf: Cf. Newton, Principia, Book I, Section III, Lemma XIV. In the configuration below, the roles of that lemma are taken as follows: F is the focus, V is the principal vertex, h1 is the tangent at the vertex, P_y is a point of the curve, m is the tangent at P_y, and P_x is the foot of the perpendicular let fall from F on that tangent.
sentences.cone_gist_ja: Menaechmus の直角円錐の切り口 — 点を通り底面に平行な平面の円で、直径に垂直な弦の半分は直径の二つの断片の比例中項(直角三角形の斜辺への垂線と同じ)。断片の一方は頂点からの距離に比例し他方は一定。ゆえに縦座標の平方は横座標に比例し、定数は latus rectum。この比例(等長ではない)が曲線の定義の性質(symptoma)。
sentences.khint: Hint: the relation in question is a mean proportional: the segment F–P_x is the mean proportional between F–V and F–P_y, that is, FPx^2 = FV·FPy, for every P_x. State the single most important invariant for E, J, K, P_y, and explain WHY it holds in a form that INCLUDES this relation.
sentences.focus_q1: Focus on the relation that holds among the following objects: {E, J, K, P_y}.
sentences.focus_q2: Focus on the relation that holds among the following objects: {F, V, P_x, P_y}.

phrases: perpendicular bisector of FK, so P_yF = P_yK

A1R.conjecture: EJ = KP_y (segment EJ always has the same length as segment KP_y)

C0.conjecture: EJ = KP_y (segment EJ has the same length as segment KP_y)

E1L.conjecture: P_y lies on the parabola with focus F and vertex V (axis j, directrix e). Equivalently, P_y F = dist(P_y, e) = P_y K, and the line m = P_y P_x is tangent to this parabola at P_y.
phrases: P_y lies on the parabola with focus F and vertex V

E1R.conjecture: FP_x^2 = FV · FP_y. Equivalently, triangles F V P_x and F P_x P_y are similar and FP_x bisects angle V F P_y. In curve form: P_y lies on the parabola with focus F and vertex V (axis FV), and P_xP_y is tangent to it at P_y.
phrases: triangles F V P_x and F P_x P_y are similar

G0.conjecture: EJ = KP_y. The segments EJ and KP_y always have equal length, and both also equal P_yF.
phrases: m is the perpendicular bisector of FK and P_yF = P_yK
P_y is equidistant from the fixed point F and the fixed line e

G1.conjecture: EJ = KP_y. The segment from E to J on the tangent g has the same length as the segment from K to P_y.

H0L.conjecture: EJ : KP_y = KP_y : EJ. The ratio is 1 : 1, so KP_y is the mean proportional between EJ and itself, which means EJ = KP_y.

H0R.conjecture: EJ : KP_y = KP_y : EJ, i.e. the ratio EJ/KP_y is 1, so EJ = KP_y for every P_x on h1. As a mean proportional: VP_x is the mean proportional between VE and VJ (VE : VP_x = VP_x : VJ). This is exactly what gives EJ = VE + VJ = KP_y.

H1.conjecture: EJ = KP_y. As a proportion: EJ : KP_y = 1 : 1. Hence EJ, like KP_y = FP_y, is the third proportional in FV : FP_x = FP_x : EJ, i.e. FP_x is a mean proportional between FV and EJ (= KP_y = FP_y), which is Newton's Lemma XIV.

H2.conjecture: |EJ| = |K P_y| (equivalently |EJ| = |F P_y|, since P_y F = P_y K)
